Explore the Andes QEMU checkout at /home/nick/work/qemu_andesim (prebuilt build at /home/nick/work/qemu_andesim/build/qemu; sources in the checkout). It is QEMU 9.x with an Andes AE350 machine model. Search breadth: very thorough.

GOAL: extract the authoritative QEMU-side guest memory map for the AE350 machine used by the andesim hybrid simulator, so it can be cross-checked against the vsim side.

Tasks:
1. Find hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c (and related: andes_plic*, andes_plmt*, atcuart/serial, any hvm/ilm/dlm device files, l2c). Extract the machine memory map: the static memmap table and/or every memory region / device instantiation with base + size, with file:line. Expect at least: main RAM (what base? how is -m / memory-backend handled?), UART(s) (which one is 0xf0300000?), SimControl/HTIF at ~0xe0080000, L2C register window at ~0xE0500000 (it seeds a reset value CEN=1 at machine init -- find that code), PLIC, PLICSW, PLMT, SMU, and anything else mapped (MAC, PIT, WDT, RTC, DMA, virtio, flash/ROM ...). Note which are real functional devices vs stub/unimplemented regions.
2. Per-CPU memories: where ILM/DLM overlays are created (CPU code, e.g. target/riscv or hw/riscv andes cpu files): their QOM property names (ilm_base/ilm_size/dlm_...?), compiled-in defaults (expect a wrong-for-everyone default like 2MB ILM at 0x0), and how the overlay attaches to the system memory. Same for HVM: device/property (hvm_size_pow_2, log2?), default base (expect 0x90000000), default size (expect 1 byte).
3. Which of these bases/sizes are configurable at runtime (QOM properties settable via -global or -readconfig), with exact property names and their defaults; quote the property definition lines.
4. Note the boot flow assumptions: where the ELF is loaded, reset vector, and whether RAM base is 0x0 or 0x80000000 for this machine.
5. If there is any existing "print the memory map" facility in this QEMU beyond the standard monitor `info mtree`, note it.

Return a structured report: one table of ALL mapped regions (name, base, size, device type, functional-vs-stub, config property if any, file:line), plus the ILM/DLM/HVM property details, plus RAM-base/boot notes. Raw data, no fluff.
